question: Which insertion, deletion, normalization and escape rules belong to canonical editing commands rather than feature-specific repair?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 23. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: An admitted input rule consumes marker and typed input in one schema-valid change; a declined rule preserves both and delegates the original insertText, insertBreak or insertData.
The actual Plite structural command and canonical schema own admission; no feature keeps a second document model or shadow validator.
Keep declarative rule priority, private trigger index, read-only matching and exactly-once next() continuation.
Plite schema stays the authority for required prefixes, defaults and validity across root and named roots.
No added hot-path machinery without a matched executable comparison.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 09-21 final-pass census, the 09-21 convergence execution and the 09-23 design and implementation receipts as historical proof. Rechecked on the live tree: InputRulesPlugin transaction/decline flow for all three commands, the decline token, createBlockStartInputRule, heading, quote, list and code-fence decline call sites, absence of canApplyBlockChanges and the deleted rule surfaces, ExitBreakPlugin and insertExitBlock, SingleBlock/SingleLine joinNextRootBlock, TrailingBlock schema construction and its nested-level test, OverridePlugin structural rule resolution, and block-void-break default construction. No tests, browser or benchmark were run.
summary: The job is predictable typing, Enter, paste and structural shorthand under installed feature policy, where an admitted rule consumes marker and input in one schema-valid change and a declined rule leaves both untouched. Live InputRulesPlugin resolves rules read-only, applies only the accepted rule inside state.transaction, and on decline() returns next() without the prefix. Heading, quote, generic block-start, list, code-fence and horizontal-rule rules delete the marker and then decline when the tx.blocks, heading or list commands return false. canApplyBlockChanges, rules.match, MatchRules, NormalizeTypesPlugin and createRuleFactory have no source matches, and exit insertion shares one private insertExitBlock. The strongest alternatives each lose (delete declarative rules for raw commands middleware, infer decline from a no-op transaction, move shorthand into Plite). Rules own trigger indexing, priority and read-only matching, a no-op is not a decline because the none action consumes input, and shorthand is product policy. Two older deferred rows remain unreproduced correctness and performance questions, namely nested block-void Enter building a root default and adjacent-text representation cleanup. Plite already exposes the nested parent default the first needs, so it is a bug-fix candidate once a probe fails, not a design pursuit.

reconciliation.question: Which insertion, deletion, normalization and escape rules belong to canonical editing commands rather than feature-specific repair?
reconciliation.reason: Live source matches its adoption claims (decline token, truthful outcomes, migrated families, deleted validator); its partial proof limits on quote/list timing and normal-size noise stay.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted atomic decline design is selected, with one candidate transaction per accepted rule, truthful command outcomes and no shadow admission path.

Deleting declarative input rules and having features author commands around() middleware directly is rejected. Rules own trigger indexing, priority, read-only matching and decline and continue composition that every feature would recopy.

Inferring decline from an empty or failed candidate transaction instead of an explicit decline() token is rejected. The none and consume outcomes legitimately produce no structural change, and command false results already reach the rule.
Moving markdown shorthand admission into Plite schema or commands is rejected. Shorthand and punctuation are Plate product policy, and Plite already owns the admission result the rule consumes.

Adding a Plite parent-aware default constructor for nested block-void Enter and exit is not a new API. public-state blocks.reset already reads schema.element(parent.type).content.default, so the deferred nested case is a bug-fix candidate once a probe reproduces it.
proofLimits: Source review only, with no package, browser or benchmark run. The implementation receipt's limits stand, namely noisy 20-block timing, no matched quote or list timing and no allocation data. The nested block-void parent-grammar case and adjacent-text representation cleanup remain unreproduced. packages/plitejs/src/core/public-state.ts and editor-schema.ts carry another session's uncommitted edits, but the cited parent-default lookup also exists at HEAD, so no decisive fact rests on them.
